title: When the mind is low
hook: chardi kala is not pretending; ask for help
tomorrow: the chemistry test comes back, and it's bad. now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, caring for the sick: seva at the bedside, and a sangat that cares for the carer. Care for the carers. Harjit slept. Simran didn't, much.
screen: `CARE FOR THE CARERS.` → `HARJIT SLEPT. SIMRAN DIDN'T.`

segments.voice: Every text Simran has sent this week ends with a smiley. Bebe's doing great! Chem test Friday, all good! Maya, who has known her since second grade, reads the smileys and sees something else. She walks over after school and finds Simran sitting in her car in the driveway, engine off, not going in. Simran says she's fine. Then she says, chardi kala, right? Then she stops talking, and doesn't start again for a while.
screen: `A SMILEY ON EVERY TEXT.` → `SITTING IN THE CAR, NOT GOING IN.` → `CHARDI KALA, RIGHT?`

segments.voice: Chardi kala comes from the close of Ardas. In paraphrase: Nanak, through the Name, may our spirits rise; by your will, may all be well. Sarbat da bhala, the good of all. Notice the shape of it. It's a request. Rising spirits are something Sikhs ask for, standing, at the close of Ardas. Not a mask you put on when you feel low, and not proof that you've failed if you can't find it. Chardi kala is not pretending. Ardas itself is the Sikh way of asking for help out loud, and asking a person is the same move, turned sideways. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: the Sikh phrase for high spirits sits inside a prayer of asking. So Simran asks. First Maya, there in the driveway: I'm not okay, I'm just tired of being the one who's okay. Then, that night, Harjit. And the next day, the school counselor, which is the hardest one. None of them fix it in a day. But the smileys stop, and the real texts start. If low ever turns into thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number, right away.
screen: `CHARDI KALA: FROM THE CLOSE OF ARDAS.` · `RISING SPIRITS ARE ASKED FOR.` · `NOT A MASK, NOT A TEST.` · `MAYA, DAD, THE COUNSELOR.` · then, large: `ASK FOR HELP.`

segments.voice: Make a small plan in your head. First, one person you could tell the truth to when your mind is low. Then the thing most likely to stop you, maybe not wanting to be a burden. Then the plan: when that thought shows up, the first words you'll say to them.
When the mind is low. Chardi kala is asked for in Ardas, not faked, and asking a person for help is part of the same prayer.
screen: `WHEN THE MIND IS LOW — today's word`.

segments.voice: Here's the line: ask for help, the way Ardas asks out loud. Day 1720, said out loud.

screen: `DAY 1720 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 94 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: THE TEST COMES BACK BAD. NOW WHAT?`

howItsDone: Sikhs ask for chardi kala at the close of Ardas, and in hard times a family may ask the sangat to include someone in its Ardas, alongside talking to friends, elders, counselors or doctors.
